newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bomb scare holds up traffic in central Wellington.
newsitem.headline: Bomb scare holds up traffic in central Wellington.

text.p: Police halted all rail and road traffic entering a part of central Wellington early on Tuesday after a beeping parcel set off a bomb scare.

Inspector Pat O'Neill of Wellington Police told Reuters that around 7.00 a.m. an employee of First Express Air New Zealand Couriers in Hutt Road discovered a package among the mail which was beeping loudly.
"He took it and ran across the road with it and put it between two big concrete pillars," O'Neill said.
The courier employee then rang police, who cordoned off the area.
Part of Thorndon Quay was cordoned off and traffic brought to a standstill. Commuter trains were also halted for the period from about 7 a.m. to 8.30 a.m.
"It had a bad effect on traffic. The Hutt Road, Thorndon Quay area is a main accessway into the city. We don't do this lighty, but obviously public safety is paramount," O'Neill said.
Those cordons had now been lifted but pedestrians were still being kept away from the area, O'Neill said.

The package had been removed from the scene and traffic was allowed through the area again. O'Neill said an explosives inspector from the Labour Department was examining the package and deciding what action to take.
"These things take time - we will hear in due course what's happening there.
"I know nothing else about the package. It's about 10 centimetres by 10 centimetres and fairly light - just a standard package," he said.
Last month, two Wellington students were injured by a parcel bomb delivered from Malaysia after collecting it from a courier company. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
